title: Residuals interlock quick scan — May 2029
content:
Purpose: Quick one-page scan to capture residual ownership and small remediation tasks for cross-functional fallback/coverage gaps discovered during the May 2029 incident runbook drill.

Summary table (rows represent one-line tracker items):
Owner | Area | Gap observed | Severity (P1-P3) | Sample metric | Proposed short fix | ETA | Status
Priya Nair | Routing | Missing secondary-region mapping for eu-west-3 | P1 | 12% of failover requests routed to default -> 2.3s additional latency | Add region fallback mapping + test: patch route table 2 | 2029-05-12 | in_progress
Marcus Li | Dedicated capacity | Oversubscription on g5 nodes during peak test | P2 | 18% request queuing at 120qps | Schedule temporary node reserve (1 pool) & autoscale tweak | 2029-05-15 | todo
Ava Torres | Console rollouts | Canary rollout not reporting early error spikes | P2 | Canary lost 4% success rate, no alerting | Wire canary -> latency/error metric alarms + paging | 2029-05-17 | todo
Benji O'Connor | KV cache | Cold cache on deploys for specific embeddings workload | P3 | TTL misses spike x6 | Add warmup job + add metric tag for cache-hit by model | 2029-05-20 | todo

Lightweight notes and rationale:
- This is intentionally compact — we want owners and single-line actions to hand off in the next standup.
- Severity heuristic: P1=customer-facing outage or SLO breach; P2=degraded perf with measurable user impact; P3=internal ops annoyance.
- Sample metrics come from quick query to observability with 90th percentile windows during the incident drill (see linked artifacts).

Immediate next steps (owner-level):
- Priya: Draft route table patch, add unit test, request infra deploy window (Slack #infra-sched). Blockers: validation cert on test region.
- Marcus: Confirm node reserve cost with finance (cc: finance ops). If >$2k/month, propose short-term cap of 2 weeks only.
- Ava: Add canary alert rule and smoke test lambda. Pair with se to get playbook for alert noise suppression.
- Benji: Prototype cache warmup script; run on staging for 48h and report cache-hit delta.

Meeting invites:
- 2029-05-11 09:30 PT: 20m sync with owners (Priya/Marcus/Ava/Benji) — goal: validate short fixes and slot deploys.
- 2029-05-14 15:00 PT: Post-fix quick validation (15m)

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we treat region fallback mapping as platform config (owned by platform-engineering) or product feature? (pri: platform)
- Can we accept a 2-week node reserve cost without formal procurement? (finance input pending)
- Should canary alert thresholds be global or per-product? (Ava to propose)

Audit trail / manual checkpoints:
- Attach quick smoke test steps in the Confluence page: INF-coverage-playbook-634.
- Record deploy window tickets: OPS-1892.

Owner sign-off lines (to be checked after fix):
- Priya: route mapping validated in staging (checkbox)
- Marcus: node reserve active and autoscaler adjusted (checkbox)
- Ava: canary alerts firing correctly and noise baseline established (checkbox)
- Benji: cache warmup reduces TTL miss spike by >=40% on staging (checkbox)

Notes to self:
- Keep this sheet short; escalate anything that grows beyond 3 line-items to dedicated postmortem.
- If any P1 remains open >72h, open an incident backlog ticket and loop SRE.

Last updated by Priya Nair on 2029-05-10 10:42 PT. Raw export: small CSV attached to Google Drive (local file id: 1a2b3c-export).
